Callers are out of my area but the helper signature matches the contract.

query-string v6.1.0 confirmed: package.json pins "query-string": "6.1.0"; node_modules/query-string/package.json version 6.1.0. Fact 1 confirmed in source: parse() ends in Object.keys(ret).sort().reduce(...) (node_modules/query-string/index.js). Fact 2 confirmed: default arrayFormat formatter does accumulator[key] = [].concat(accumulator[key], value) (occurrence order), and the final reduce's keysSorter guard is `Boolean(value) && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)` — arrays take the else branch untouched. Rule 1's value[0] = first occurrence therefore holds.

Key-decoder agreement: helper does param.replace(/\+/g, " ").split("=")[0] then decodeUriComponent(rawKey); parse does param.replace(/\+/g, ' ').split('=') then decode(key) -> decodeComponent = the same decode-uri-component v0.2.0 module. Identical pre-replacement, identical split, identical decoder on the identical string — byte-for-byte agreement on every key. Six adversarial traces run on paper (see notes).

Output contract: trackingParams.utmSource/utmCampaign/internalRef set only when parsedParams[<snake key>] !== undefined; utmData filter is key.indexOf('utm_') === 0 && key !== 'utm_source' && key !== 'utm_campaign' && parsedParams[key] !== undefined — excludes exactly the two named params; keys stored raw (decoded param name, not camelCased); every utmData value routed through sanitizeTrackingValue.
Rule 1: sanitizeTrackingValue takes isArray(value) ? value[0] : value — first occurrence, valid per verified fact 2.

Rule 2 (amended): code slices to TRACKING_VALUE_MAX_LENGTH (255), reads charCodeAt(length-1), and slices off a final code unit iff it is in 0xD800-0xDBFF — exactly the amended §5.1 rule 2. On the contract input (location.search is a USVString: browsers percent-encode and never surface lone surrogates), the only reachable trailing-high-surrogate case is a slice-split pair, so the spec's 'left when the slice splits a surrogate pair' wording covers all reachable behavior, and the post-drop string can never end in another unpaired surrogate (unit 253 of a USVString whose unit 254 is a high surrogate is necessarily BMP or the low half of a complete pair).

Rule 3: utmDataKeys = keysInOccurrenceOrder.filter(...).slice(0, UTM_DATA_MAX_KEYS) with UTM_DATA_MAX_KEYS = 10 — first 10 by raw-string occurrence order, dedupe on first occurrence via indexOf === -1 push.

Absence semantics: absent param -> parsedParams key undefined -> field never set (no || fallbacks anywhere in the helper); utmData attached only inside if (utmDataKeys.length > 0); valueless ?utm_source -> parse yields null -> null !== undefined -> sanitizeTrackingValue(null) returns null unchanged (isString guard) -> utmSource: null passes through; non-string values are returned untouched, nothing fabricated.

Placement + imports: sanitizeTrackingParams sits immediately after standardizeQueryParamsObject at the top of utils.js; imports `queryString from "query-string"` and `decodeUriComponent from "decode-uri-component"` added at the top (diff lines +5-6).

notes: Adversarial decoder traces (scan vs parse, identical outcome in all): (1) '?utm_zzz=1&utm_%73ource=A&utm_aaa=2&utm_source=B' — %73 decodes to 's', both paths key it as utm_source; utmSource='A' (first occurrence), utmData={utm_zzz,utm_aaa} in occurrence order. (2) '+' in key: '?utm_camp+aign=X' — both pre-replace '+' to space before decoding, key 'utm_camp aign' in both, captured into utmData consistently; '%5F' ('?utm%5Fsource=Y') decodes to utm_source in both, correctly excluded from utmData and captured as utmSource. (3) malformed sequence + valueless + empty segments: '?&utm_medium&utm_%E4=x&&utm_content=c' — decodeURIComponent throws on '%E4', decode-uri-component's fallback leaves 'utm_%E4' literal in BOTH paths (same module), so scan key === parse key; utm_medium (valueless) parses to null and lands in utmData as null (§5.1/§5.3 acknowledge null pass-through); empty segments: helper skips them, parse keys them as '' (never utm_-prefixed) — no capture difference. (4) '%2B' in key decodes to literal '+' (not space) in both paths — the '+'-replacement precedes percent-decoding identically. (5) '%3D'/'%26' in keys survive the pre-decode '='/'&' splits identically in both paths. (6) repeated differently-encoded same key dedupes to the first raw occurrence, matching parse's array order. Only divergence found: parse trims the whole input and strips one leading [?#&] while the helper slices after '?', so inputs with leading/trailing whitespace or without '?' behave differently — unreachable for the contract input (WHATWG URL puts U+0020 in the query percent-encode set and location.search is a USVString beginning with '?' or empty); this is the settled LOW 4 degenerate-input family, not flagged per the brief. Also checked and conforming: parsedParams is Object.create(null) (no prototype-chain false positives in the undefined checks); a literal '?utm_data=x' param lands inside utmData keyed 'utm_data' per the every-other-utm_ rule; sanitizeTrackingValue as an unexported inner helper is within §5.1's stated plan-level mechanism latitude and is the l2-B1-sanctioned code. One neutral observation, not a finding: approved-decisions.md line 17 (D4) still reads 'truncated to 255 characters' — the l1-run4-001 fix was explicitly scoped to SPEC.md only (FAILURE-REPORT hard constraints) and the brief designates the spec as the Layer 1 authority. decode-uri-component remains a transitive dependency of query-string (settled LOW, phantom-dependency ruling — unflagged). utils.js at HEAD fc3f047f9 matches the pre-dumped diff hunk exactly.
